summary: The root أدد primarily signifies something great, mighty, or severe. It can refer to a great calamity or a severe, distressing event.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: أَدَّتَّةُ دَاهِيَةٌ, aor اَدُدَ (T, S; M, K) and اَدِدَ, (M, K,) but this latter is strange, [anomalous,] and unknown, (TA,) and اَدَدَ, (M, K,) mentioned by Lh, whence it seems that he made the pret. to be of the measure فَعِلَ, or that it is co-ordinate to أَبَى, aor يَأْبَى, (M,) inf. n. أَدُّ, (T, S, M,) A calamity befell him. (M, K.) And in like manner, أَدَّهُ أَمْرٌ, aor. and inf. n. as above, An event befell him: (M:) or oppressed him, distressed him, or afflicted him. (Bd in xix.
تأدّد; (T, K;) and, inf. n. أَدُّ; (TA;) i. q. تَشَدَّدَ [ He acted, or behaved, with forced hardness, firmness, strength, vigour, &c. ]. (T, K.)

أَدُّ (S, M, K) and (T, K) and (K) Strength; power; force: (S, M, K:) superior power or force or influence; mastery; conquest; predominance. (M, K, TA.) See also إِدُّ, in two places. Also, the first, The sound of treading. (T.)

إِدُّ أد إد اد ودى آد: see أَدُّ. Also, and, A wonder, or wonderful thing: (M, L, K:) a very evil, abominable, severe, thing, or affair: (S, M, A, L, K:) a calamity; (S, A, L, K,) or thus the former word signifies; (M;) as also, (as in the copies of the K,) or, [originally آدِدً ] of the measure فَاعِلْ: (so in the S and L:) pl. (of إِدُّ M, TA) إِدادُ (K, TA,) or أَدَادُ (T, CK, [but this, if correct, is a quasi-pl.
إِدَّةٌ أد أده إد إده اده ادة دهى دهي ودى آد آده: see إِدُّ in two places.
آدُّ آد: see أَدُّ: and see إِدُّ in two places.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
